stats.fact: mem-port uses embedded SurrealDB combining graph storage and vector search — no external Postgres, Qdrant, or Neo4j required
Supports Streamable HTTP transport with library-id header for multi-tenant isolation (personal/team/project scopes)

Provides 12 MCP tools: save_memory, search_memory, save_episode, list_episodes, save_skill, search_skills, list_skills, get_skill, forget_skill, get_entity, relate_entities, forget_memory, export_library, import_library
Export/import system produces portable .memport.json bundles — plain JSON, commitable to git, movable between machines
engram (5,778 stars) is the most popular MCP memory project — Go binary with SQLite + FTS5
MCP (Model Context Protocol) ecosystem has 1,182+ repositories tagged with memory/server on GitHub as of August 2026
mem-port uses local embedding model (Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2) — no API key needed for semantic search
mem-port is MIT licensed, written in TypeScript, published as npm package @rsl-innovation/mem-port

angles: Zero-external-dependency architecture — embedded SurrealDB replaces Postgres + vector DB + graph DB stack
Portable memory as a thumb drive metaphor — export/import .memport.json bundles between machines
Multi-copilot shared memory — Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf all read/write the same graph simultaneously
Skills as portable procedures — save a skill once, available to every connected copilot without file conversion
Three-scope architecture (personal/team/project) using library-id isolation — keeps context cleanly separated
No API key required for semantic search — fully local embedding model
launchd/systemd service setup for persistent daemon — survives reboots and crashes
